plate_findings.evidence: Caption: 'corneal hydrops in advanced keratoconus showing corneal edema at the apex of the cone.'
Caption identifies the edematous region as being 'at the apex of the cone.'
Caption explicitly reports 'increased corneal thickness' as the reverse of thinning, so central thinning is not supported.

findings.evidence: Caption: 'corneal hydrops in advanced keratoconus showing corneal edema at the apex of the cone.'

panels.stage: acute corneal hydrops in advanced keratoconus
panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Real human slit-lamp photograph showing the captioned acute corneal hydrops associated with advanced keratoconus. [raw subtype: advanced keratoconus with acute corneal hydrops] B: Narrow slit-lamp view of the same real patient's acute corneal hydrops in advanced keratoconus. [raw subtype: advanced keratoconus with acute corneal hydrops] C: Patient anterior-segment OCT demonstrates pronounced ectasia, corneal thickening, and fluid-filled stromal clefts corresponding to acute hydrops. [raw subtype: advanced keratoconus with acute corneal hydrops]
panels.attribution_text: Moramarco et al. Air-Assisted Dome Drainage in Acute Corneal Hydrops: A 3D-OCT-Guided Approach.. Bioengineering (Basel, Switzerland) 2025. doi:10.3390/bioengineering12080867. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Acute corneal hydrops of the case highlighted. (A) Slit-lamp diffuse illumination view of corneal hydrops in advanced keratoconus showing corneal edema at the apex of the cone. (B) Narrow slit-lamp view of image (A). (C) Anterior segment optical coherence tomography showing a pronounced corneal ectasia with increased corneal thickness. The intrastromal hyporeflective spaces are consistent with stromal edema secondary to aqueous influx through the rupture.
in_text_mentions: He had no history of previous cross-linking or other corneal surgery. Pre-operative AS-OCT highlighted the DM tear with stromal thickening and multiple hyporeflective intrastomal clefts filled with fluid (Figure 3).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: Representative patient AS-OCT in an article specifically about keratoconus demonstrates the captioned posterior corneal protrusion. B: Patient anterior tangential curvature map directly shows localized inferocentral corneal steepening characteristic of keratoconus. C: The caption identifies superior-inferior asymmetry and significant coma in a representative keratoconus case. These specific findings are not in the supplied vocabulary, so they are proposed findings. D: The patient corneal thickness map demonstrates asymmetric, decentered corneal thinning consistent with keratoconus. E: The posterior elevation map from the representative keratoconus case shows the captioned focal asymmetric elevation, a keratoconus-associated manifestation not represented in the provided vocabulary.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: Representative human keratoconus AS-OCT image showing apical stromal scarring and focal surface flattening at the cone apex. [raw subtype: irregular halo sign] B: Representative keratoconus anterior tangential curvature map showing localized concentric corneal steepening. [raw subtype: irregular halo sign] C: Representative keratoconus HOA map illustrating profound optical-system irregularity, a described manifestation associated with the irregular halo sign phenotype. [raw subtype: irregular halo sign] D: Representative keratoconus corneal thickness map showing localized, eccentrically positioned thinning. [raw subtype: irregular halo sign] E: Representative keratoconus posterior elevation map showing focal ectatic elevation of the posterior cornea. [raw subtype: irregular halo sign]

panels.figure_caption: Imaging of a Representative Case with an Irregular Halo Sign (Group B, HMI = 3.53). B, The tangential curvature map shows an expanded area of concentric steepening compared with the case in Fig. 5. C, The HOA map illustrates profound optical system irregularity. D, The corneal thickness map shows a localized area of thinning with an eccentrically positioned thinnest region. E, The posterior corneal elevation map shows a focal posterior elevation pattern corresponding to the ectatic region
